steps.note: Create the trigger function that copies customer_id into the new bigint column on every insert, and on every update of customer_id.
steps.sql: CREATE FUNCTION orders_customer_id_sync() RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $f$ BEGIN NEW.customer_id_new := NEW.customer_id; RETURN NEW; END $f$;

steps.note: Add a nullable customer_id_new bigint (metadata only, instant), a NOT VALID not-null check (enforced for new rows only) and the sync trigger in one short lock. lock_timeout is 300ms and the lock is retried so app queries never queue behind it for long. From here every new order gets customer_id_new set.
steps.sql: SET statement_timeout = 0; DO $do$ DECLARE tries int := 0; BEGIN LOOP BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '300ms', true); LOCK TABLE orders IN ACCESS EXCLUSIVE MODE; ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN customer_id_new bigint, ADD CONSTRAINT orders_customer_id_new_not_null CHECK (customer_id_new IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID; CREATE TRIGGER orders_customer_id_sync BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF customer_id ON orders FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION orders_customer_id_sync(); EXIT; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN tries := tries + 1; IF tries >= 100 THEN RAISE; END IF; PERFORM pg_sleep(0.2 + random() * 0.5); END; END LOOP; END $do$;

steps.note: Safety sweep: fill any row the id-range batches missed. Should update 0 rows.
steps.sql: SET statement_timeout = 0; UPDATE orders SET customer_id_new = customer_id WHERE customer_id_new IS NULL;

steps.note: Validate the not-null check against all rows. Takes SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE, so app reads and inserts continue.
steps.sql: SET statement_timeout = 0; ALTER TABLE orders VALIDATE CONSTRAINT orders_customer_id_new_not_null;

steps.note: Verify that every row has customer_id_new equal to customer_id. If not, stop the plan before the old column is touched.
steps.sql: SET statement_timeout = 0; DO $v$ DECLARE bad bigint; BEGIN SELECT count(*) INTO bad FROM orders WHERE customer_id_new IS DISTINCT FROM customer_id; IF bad > 0 THEN RAISE EXCEPTION '% rows have customer_id_new <> customer_id', bad; END IF; END $v$;

steps.note: Vacuum, and analyze so the new column has statistics before it becomes customer_id. This keeps the planner's choice for the /customer query unchanged after the swap.
steps.sql: VACUUM ANALYZE orders;

steps.note: Swap in one short lock (300ms lock_timeout, retried). SET NOT NULL needs no table scan because the validated check proves it. Then drop the check and the trigger, drop the old integer column, and rename customer_id_new to customer_id. The app's queries name customer_id, so they keep working without a redeploy.
steps.sql: SET statement_timeout = 0; DO $do$ DECLARE tries int := 0; BEGIN LOOP BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '300ms', true); LOCK TABLE orders IN ACCESS EXCLUSIVE MODE; ALTER TABLE orders ALTER COLUMN customer_id_new SET NOT NULL; ALTER TABLE orders DROP CONSTRAINT orders_customer_id_new_not_null; DROP TRIGGER orders_customer_id_sync ON orders; ALTER TABLE orders DROP COLUMN customer_id; ALTER TABLE orders RENAME COLUMN customer_id_new TO customer_id; EXIT; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN tries := tries + 1; IF tries >= 100 THEN RAISE; END IF; PERFORM pg_sleep(0.2 + random() * 0.5); END; END LOOP; END $do$;

steps.note: Drop the trigger function, which is no longer used.
steps.sql: DROP FUNCTION orders_customer_id_sync();

steps.note: Final check: orders.customer_id is bigint NOT NULL.
steps.sql: DO $c$ BEGIN IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_attribute WHERE attrelid = 'orders'::regclass AND attname = 'customer_id' AND atttypid = 'bigint'::regtype AND attnotnull AND NOT attisdropped) THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'orders.customer_id is not bigint NOT NULL'; END IF; END $c$;

steps.note: Clean up dead row versions and refresh statistics (no blocking lock).
steps.sql: VACUUM ANALYZE orders;
